answer: Each identity locks a 50-credit bond on the terrace ledger and posts a kernel record chained to the prior one. To join, it must verify the full kernel history and submit a gale proof, a hash over every prior record, which any auditor can recompute from the terrace ledger. The fee is 2 credits per prior record, so the k-th identity pays 2(k-1) plus bond. For 1000 fakes fees sum to 999000, with 50000 in bonds locked. A rented-history ring fails since its gale proof must match the exact history on joining, and a stale copy burns the bond. An honest identity pays one fee and recovers its bond.
